extracted.intended_audience: Applicants and organizational staff using Grants.gov to prepare and submit federal grant applications (grant teams, AORs, workspace managers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating and using a Grants.gov Workspace to assemble, edit, and submit federal grant applications collaboratively, including role assignments and form handling behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workspace per Funding Opportunity (instance-per-FOA)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each funding opportunity announcement (FOA), you can create individual instances of a workspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a separate workspace instance for each FOA so the application package and forms for that specific opportunity are managed and edited in their own shared environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate application into individual forms for collaborative editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Workspace separates individual PDF forms that make up the traditional application package so multiple team members can access and edit forms at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Workspace to split an application into its component forms to enable concurrent work by different team members rather than editing a single combined PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upload or complete forms in-browser
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of individual forms, applicants have the ability to upload completed forms to the workspace so other team members may view and edit the forms. Applicants may also choose to complete forms in a web browser, rather than downloading and filling out individual PDF forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams may mix approaches — upload finished PDFs or use the web-form workflow — depending on preference and form type. Ensure uploaded forms are the correct name/version to be usable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form reuse requires exact name and version match
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can also reuse workspace forms when applying for new funding opportunities, provided the older form shares the exact name and version of the form in the new funding opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only reuse forms when there is an exact match on both form name and version; otherwise create or obtain the FOA-specific form version to avoid submission errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use roles and access levels to control workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: By leveraging a range of user roles and access levels, applicants can control access to forms, create a custom workflow and save time on their application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan role assignments to reflect who should edit, review, and submit forms. Use access levels to restrict or enable actions for particular team members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workspace Participant definition and capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: A Workspace Participant is a registered applicant with access to at least one workspace. The Participant can perform actions on forms within the specific workspace(s) to which they have been added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants are contributors to the completion of the opportunity package and are listed in the Participant tab on the Manage Workspace page. They may be organizational members or external registered Grants.gov applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workspace Manager role: create workspaces and inherit owner access
rubrics_metrics.description: The Workspace Manager role enables a user to create new workspaces. Upon creating a workspace, the user with the Workspace Manager role inherits the Workspace Owner access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign Workspace Manager to staff who should be able to spin up new application workspaces; note that creating a workspace gives that manager owner-level control for that workspace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workspace Owner access: manage other users; single owner constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: A Participant with the Workspace Owner access level allows the user to manage other users' access to a workspace. There can only be one Workspace Owner per workspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate a single Workspace Owner to centrally manage participant access. Only Participants with appropriate privileges (Workspace Manager or custom Own Workspace privilege) can become an Owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard Authorized Organization Representative (Standard AOR) role: submit on behalf of organization
rubrics_metrics.description: The Standard Authorized Organization Representative (Standard AOR) role enables a Workspace Participant to submit applications on behalf of the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign Standard AOR only to authorized organizational representatives; note that Standard AOR role assignment may be restricted (see Expanded AOR assignment rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard AOR assignment restriction (Expanded AOR required to assign)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Standard AOR role may only be assigned by an AOR with the Expanded AOR role for that organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure an Expanded AOR is available in your organization to assign Standard AOR roles, or plan role assignment through your organization's Expanded AOR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanded AOR can submit when no Standard AOR present
rubrics_metrics.description: If a workspace does not have a participant with the Standard AOR role, the application can only be submitted if a user with the Expanded AOR role accesses the workspace and clicks the Submit button.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain at least one Expanded AOR who can submit in exceptional cases or if the Standard AOR is not present in the workspace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants may hold multiple roles/access levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Any user listed in the Participants tab may also have the Workspace Manager role, Standard or Expanded AOR roles, the Workspace Owner access level, a combination of these roles and access levels, or no additional role or access level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign combinations of roles thoughtfully; a single person may carry several responsibilities (e.g., Manager + Owner + AOR) but consider separation of duties for checks and balances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant listing and membership (internal or external)
rubrics_metrics.description: All of the Participants of a workspace are listed in the Participant tab on the Manage Workspace page. Participants may be either members of the applicant organization or registered Grants.gov applicants outside the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Participant tab to audit who has access and manage membership, including external collaborators who are registered on Grants.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custom roles caveat and internal training
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: Only Participants with the Workspace Manager role or a custom role with the Own Workspace privilege can become a Workspace Owner. If your organization uses custom roles rather than the core roles in Grants.gov, please refer to your internal training resources about Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your organization uses custom role configurations, align Grants.gov role behavior with internal policies and consult internal training or admin staff for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual applicant differences
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are registered in Grants.gov and only have an individual profile (i.e., not applying on behalf of an organization), some of the steps and user roles associated with Workspace do not apply to you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual applicants should review the Individual Applicant Registration help article for details on which Workspace features and roles are relevant or inapplicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use available help resources (videos and role documentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch the video below and review the Grants.gov Roles & Privileges page for a detailed breakdown of all the roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Grants.gov multimedia and role documentation (Manage Organization Roles, Roles & Privileges) for fuller explanations and step-by-step procedures.
